title: Gratin de Chou-Fleur
subtitle: Cauliflower baked in a gruyere bechamel with a golden crumb
excerpt: Cauliflower florets are coated in a rich gruyere bechamel, topped with breadcrumbs and more cheese, and baked until bubbling and golden. The sauce sets around the cauliflower and every spoonful has crunch on top and creaminess underneath.
sourceNotes: Classic French gratin technique applied to cauliflower. Synthesised from standard bechamel gratin methods taught across French culinary tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the gratin up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the oven time.

content.text: A gratin is one of the most satisfying things you can make with a cauliflower. The bechamel is the part that needs attention. Whisk constantly once the milk goes in or it will go lumpy.
Heat the oven to 200C. Bring the large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the cauliflower and cook for 5 minutes until just barely tender. Drain well and spread in a single layer to steam dry.
Melt the butter in the medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the warm milk in a slow stream, whisking constantly. Return to a medium heat and whisk until the sauce is smooth and thick, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 80g of the gruyere, the mustard, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Arrange the cauliflower in the gratin dish. Pour the bechamel evenly over the top, making sure all the florets are coated.
Mix the remaining 40g gruyere with the breadcrumbs. Scatter evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is deep golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The milk was added too fast or the pan was too hot.
items.fix: Pass the sauce through a sieve, pressing with the back of a spoon, then whisk hard over low heat to smooth it.

items.symptom: The topping is golden but the sauce underneath is watery.
items.cause: The cauliflower was not drained well enough before assembling.
items.fix: Let the gratin rest for 5 minutes out of the oven. The sauce will firm as it cools slightly.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning or the flour was not cooked out fully.
items.fix: Add more dijon mustard and season with salt and pepper. A little extra grated cheese stirred in will also help.
